page: Microsoft Azure L32s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 256.0 GB, allocating 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. Local storage is provided through 7,680 GB of bundled NVMe SSD capacity, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent.

Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core processing and high throughput capabilities. The system ranks in the top 25% for both Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, alongside strong performance in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth at 197.62 GB/sec. Hardware acceleration via Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions contributes to top-tier image processing metrics and rapid prompt processing on smaller machine learning models. Workloads involving larger models, such as 70B parameter generation, reflect weaker output rates due to reliance solely on CPU execution.

The dense pairing of 7.68 TB local NVMe storage and 256 GB of RAM provides favorable cost efficiency for I/O-heavy operations by eliminating reliance on external network volumes for fast data access. This makes the L32s_v4 suitable for transactional databases, NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, and static web serving architectures.
description: Microsoft Azure L32s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance features 256.0 GB of system memory, an extensive 260 MB L3 cache, and 7,680 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, with no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and throughput characteristics, including top 25% Geekbench scores, high uncached memory read bandwidth of 197.62 GB/sec, and fast multi-threaded compression metrics. Supported by Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions, it performs well on smaller machine learning inference models and image processing tasks. Combining dense local solid-state storage with generous memory-per-core sizing, the L32s_v4 provides a cost-effective, high-throughput foundation for storage-bound applications, including relational and NoSQL databases, search indexers, and distributed file processing clusters.
